title: Understanding Humidity-Enhanced Adhesion of Geckos: Deep Neural Network-Assisted Multi-Scale Molecular Modeling
summary: A deep neural network parameterized a mesoscale keratin model from atomistic elastic properties, enabling simulations of gecko spatula adhesion under different humidity conditions. In the model, water-induced softening alone modestly increased pull-off on flat hydrophobic surfaces, while it contributed more on nanostructured surfaces by improving conformity. This isolates a modeled contribution and does not explain the full humidity effect.
ai_technology: A deep neural network predicts mesoscale bonded-force-field coefficients from target elastic constants derived using atomistic keratin simulations, enabling efficient parameterization of the whole-spatula simulations that quantify humidity-dependent adhesion.
organization: University of Akron; University of California San Diego

source_review.scope: Primary source full text, including Methods and Results; first result-bearing version checked against primary publication metadata.

evidence.tested: Ten independently generated simulations per condition compared 0%, 5%, 10% and 20% water; modeled softening raised pull-off by about 10% on flat hydrophobic surfaces and up to 120% on nanostructured surfaces at high water content.
evidence.unknown: Multiscale simulations are model-dependent and address a softening contribution; they do not establish that softening alone explains the observed humidity-associated adhesion increase.
evidence.ai_role: A deep neural network predicts mesoscale bonded-force-field coefficients from target elastic constants derived using atomistic keratin simulations, enabling efficient parameterization of the whole-spatula simulations that quantify humidity-dependent adhesion.
